masks.why: wall clock (Node adds it to every response)

masks.where: request heads, header values, bodies, frames, logs, env: the den port after `:` or `: ` (and the value of `RIVETOS_DEN_PORT`)
masks.why: each den listens on a fresh free port; the harness substitutes the real port into `{{PORT}}` when it sends
per-run temp root (state dirs, static dir, mesh/users files, PKI)
absolute path of the node binary
machine hostname; `bodyLength` is null and `bodyMasked` true on such bodies

masks.where: any 13-digit number within 7 days of the harness start (in practice only `timestamp:` in the RivetError dump of the mesh.json 500 log line)
masks.why: wall clock; fixture event timestamps are 2025 values (1760000000000+) and are never masked

conventions: request.head is the exact request head sent (CRLF line ends); {{PORT}} is replaced by the real port when sent.
response.headers are [name, value] pairs in wire order and wire case; values are OWS-trimmed (rawHeaderLines appears only if a line was not "Name: value").
response.body is the exact payload after de-chunking (utf8 text, or bodyBase64 when not valid UTF-8); framing says how it was delimited on the wire and chunks how many data chunks Node wrote.
serverClosed: the den closed the connection after the response (observed for 120 ms, or 1500 ms when the response says Connection: close or is a 413); keep-alive responses stay open.
noResponse: the den closed or destroyed the socket without writing any bytes.

log: den stdout/stderr lines emitted while the case ran, minus the lines the 5 s peer-origin refresh can print at any time (mesh roster unreadable / skipping invalid node / ignoring node); those strings are recorded once, deterministically, in startup.json.
"remote" callers connect to 127.0.0.1 from source address 127.0.0.2; the den only treats 127.0.0.1, ::1 and ::ffff:127.0.0.1 as loopback.
inventory: the status the inventory (/rivet-shared/plans/rust-rewrite/inventory/gateway-api.md) states for this case, and whether the recording matches it.

tls-main.description: HTTPS on 0.0.0.0 with RIVETOS_DEN_TLS_CERT/KEY/CA (client cert requested and verified, never rejected at the TLS layer); static dir; no users.json. "remote" callers dial 127.0.0.1 from source 127.0.0.2, which the den treats as non-loopback.

Device certificate required

This gateway only accepts enrolled devices. Clicking through the padlock / certificate warning trusts the server CA — it is not a client certificate.
